sentences.text:
This application coming on for hearing this day, the cou  following:
 ORDER

This second application has been filed by applicant under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.593 of 2023 registered at Police Station Chachoda, District Guna (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 302, 201 and added Section 376 (D) of IPC.
Applicant is in judicial custody since 06-12-2023.
First application was dismissed as withdrawn by this Court vide order dated 22.03.2024 passed in MCRC No.9534/2024.
Thereafter, statements of prosecution witnesses were recorded.
As per the case of prosecution, dead body of one unknown lady was found in decomposed condition from a culvert near village Badkua.
She was identified as Sukhia Bai W/o Kishan Lal Lodhi.
Postmortem examination was conducted on dead body of Sukhia Bai.
Medical Officer opined that she died due to cardio respiratory arrest, but no certain opinion about mode of death was given.

P.S.
Chachoda registered FIR at Crime No. 593 of 2023 for offence punishable U/ss. 302 and 201 of IPC against unknown offender.
During investigation, Jainarayan Lodhi, Rekam Lodhi and Dhapu Bai stated that Pintiya alias Rambharose Lodhi was consuming liquor with him.

sentences.text: Thereafter, Pintiya and Mahendra (present applicant) left his house.
Around 4:00 in the morning, he saw Pintiya and Mahendra Lodhi taking a lady on their motorcycle.
After one hour, Mahendra and Pintiya returned.
Jaynarayan overheard Mahendra and Pintiya discussing rape with that lady.
Accordingly, Mahendra, Pintiya and Harinarayan were taken into custody.
Their statements U/s 27 of the Evidence Act were recorded.
Mobile phone was recovered and seized at the instance of the applicant.
On completion of investigation, final report was submitted on 31.12.2023.
The trial is underway.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant is falsely implicated in the matter merely on the basis of statements of Jainarayan Lodhi, Rekam and Dhapu Bai.
No incriminating evidence is available against the applicant.

Learned Counsel referring to statements of Rajan (PW/1), Rekam (PW/2), Dhapu Bai (PW/3) and Jainaryan (PW/4) recorded before the Trial Court submits that none of the prosecution witnesses have supported the prosecution.
The fate of prosecution against the applicant is apparent.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is aged around 20 years and is an agriculturist by profession.
There is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family, home and profession.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
There is no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence by the applicant.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the young applicant.
Trial would take time to conclude.

Co-accused Rambharosa @ Pintu has been extended benefit of bail by this Court vide order dated 10.05.2024 passed in MCRC No.16344/2024 and the case of the applicant is almost identical to that of co-accused.
Therefore, on the ground of parity, the applicant may also be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and prays for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, regard being had to the young age of the applicant, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
